answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity commits a signed forecast vector at epoch start; at close, agents whose revealed behaviour diverges from their prior trajectory beyond a fixed tolerance are weight-capped. Consistency must hold across a trellis of overlapping epochs, not one. A sonnet of past epochs, so to speak, is compared. An attacker splitting into many fresh identities must sustain coherent behaviour through a canyon of consecutive epochs before gaining full weight, paying full compute and compliance cost per identity throughout.
